elements.element: No obligation on Customer to disclose more favourable third-party commercial offers to Vendor
elements.evidence: "Customer is not required to disclose or match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives"

elements.element: No obligation on Customer to match a third party's more favourable offer for Vendor's benefit
elements.evidence: "is not required to disclose or match"

elements.element: No condition/precondition on Customer engaging another provider (i.e., MFN not triggered by sourcing elsewhere)
elements.evidence: "Before engaging another provider, Customer is not required to..." — the pre-engagement duty is negated

elements.element: MFN obligation limited to a single defined product/service
elements.evidence: No MFN obligation remains at all; clause negates rather than scopes: "is not required to disclose or match"

elements.element: MFN obligation limited to a 12-month duration
elements.evidence: No duration language anywhere in revised 7.2
No comparison carve-out language in revised 7.2

reasons: The single replacement converts the disclose-and-match duty into an express statement that Customer bears no such obligation, satisfying the preferred position that no MFN burden fall on Customer.
Minimal: only the operative duty phrase was swapped for its negation; no new exceptions, defined terms, or boilerplate were added, and the rest of Section 7 is untouched.
Intent preserved: no undefined terms or dangling mechanics are created, and the change aligns 7.2 with Section 12.3's no-most-favoured-customer acknowledgement rather than contradicting it.

Fallback is not satisfied (no scoped product, 12-month term, or comparison carve-outs), but that is irrelevant since the locked preferred level is met and the preferred level is more favourable to Customer.

Optional polish only: the retained lead-in "Before engaging another provider" could be read as time-limiting the negation; deleting the sentence or the lead-in would remove any residual implication, but this is a drafting nit, not a substantive gap.
